hero.headline: Inflation Rises to 4.2 Percent as Fed Rate Cut Grows Unlikely
hero.body:
Consumer prices rose 4.2 percent in May compared to a year earlier, reaching the highest inflation rate in three years and clouding prospects for Federal Reserve interest rate cuts. The timing creates an immediate challenge for Kevin M. Warsh as he begins his tenure as Fed chair, with his first policy meeting scheduled for the following week.

The inflation increase reflects mounting pressures on the economy, particularly from energy markets. Energy prices accounted for 60 percent of the monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index. The national average gas price stood at $4.15 per gallon, roughly one dollar higher than a year ago. Airline fares jumped 26.7 percent annually, while food, energy services, and clothing also saw price increases. When stripping out volatile energy and food prices, core inflation rose to 2.9 percent.

The jump marks the third consecutive monthly increase since the start of the U.S.-Israel war with Iran. Inflation stood at just 2.4 percent in February, before the conflict began. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted energy supplies and driven prices upward across the economy.

The May reading exceeds the Federal Reserve's two percent inflation target by a significant margin. Fed officials have stated they need sustained evidence of inflation returning to their target before considering rate reductions. Higher inflation typically requires maintaining or raising interest rates rather than cutting them.

President Trump responded to the inflation data by saying he loves the numbers, attributing lower oil prices to military actions against Iran. A White House spokesperson characterized the inflation figures as "at-expectation" and pointed to declines in prescription drug prices, dairy products, and auto insurance as evidence that the administration's economic agenda continues delivering results.

However, higher prices have dampened Americans' financial outlook. A Federal Reserve Bank of New York survey released Monday showed households growing more pessimistic about inflation, the job market, and potential layoffs. Consumer sentiment has hit historic lows after falling for three consecutive months.

Financial markets reacted negatively to the inflation report, with stock indexes opening lower as investors adjusted expectations for monetary policy. Extended high interest rates can reduce corporate profits and stock valuations while increasing borrowing costs for businesses and consumers.

The labor market remains relatively strong, with employers adding 172,000 jobs in May and unemployment holding at 4.3 percent. Goldman Sachs said Friday it no longer expected the Fed to cut rates this year, instead predicting unchanged rates through 2026 with cuts potentially delayed until 2027. JPMorgan Global Research predicted the Fed might increase rates by 2027, particularly as global central banks reassess their monetary policy paths.

cards.headline: Trump Threatens to Strike Iran Again After Weeks of Shifting Signals
cards.body:
President Trump said the United States would hit Iran "hard" again, warning Tehran "will have to pay the price" for delaying negotiations on a potential agreement. The threat came after the president claimed Iran was "playing us for suckers" by drawing out talks, though he provided no specifics about what terms were being discussed or what would trigger the promised strikes.

The renewed military threat followed a day in which Trump had expressed optimism about reaching a deal, marking another sharp reversal in the administration's messaging on Iran. According to a CNN analysis, Trump has claimed a deal was "close" at least 38 times since the conflict began, yet no agreement has materialized. This pattern of oscillating between threats of escalation and predictions of imminent peace has characterized the administration's approach to Iran for weeks, leaving both allies and adversaries uncertain about whether the U.S. intends to pursue diplomacy or military action.

The latest escalation occurred after the U.S. military fired on an oil tanker called the Settebello in the Gulf of Oman. The vessel was attempting to transport oil from Iran in violation of a U.S. blockade on Iranian ports. The strike resulted in three Indian sailors going missing and 21 crew members being rescued, prompting a diplomatic protest from India. The incident underscores how the ongoing conflict continues to disrupt international shipping and regional stability.

In response to the latest American threats, Tehran vowed retaliation for any new attacks. Iranian officials have not publicly addressed the specific timeline or conditions Trump referenced in his recent statements. The conflict has already disrupted oil transport through the Gulf, a crucial waterway for global energy supplies, contributing to rising inflation that has reached 4.2 percent annually as of May, according to recent data.

Pentagon investigations into military operations in the conflict have raised questions about targeting procedures and intelligence accuracy. Military planners generate target lists from databases using artificial intelligence tools, but it remains unclear whether each target was verified before strikes were carried out. Designating buildings as targets involves specialized analysts working years in advance with layers of oversight, though targets may not be reviewed again until a strike is considered.

White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said in a statement that investigations into specific incidents are ongoing, noting that "unlike the terrorist Iranian regime, the United States does not target civilians."

The uncertainty surrounding U.S. policy has left international observers struggling to predict whether the administration will ultimately pursue a negotiated settlement or continue military operations. Trump's comments suggested growing frustration with negotiating timelines, but the administration has disclosed limited details about what a potential agreement would require or what steps Iran must take to avoid further military action.

cards.headline: IDF Strikes Kill 30 in Lebanon, Health Ministry Reports
cards.teaser: Israeli military operations in Lebanon resulted in 30 deaths over the past day, according to the Lebanese health ministry.
cards.body:
Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed 30 people over the past 24 hours, the Lebanese health ministry reported. Israel ordered residents of the ancient coastal city of Tyre to evacuate, though at least one deadly strike hit the city before the warning was issued.

Satellite images showed destruction in the historical city of Tyre, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

cards.headline: U.S. Strike on Tanker Near Oman Leaves Three Indian Sailors Missing
cards.teaser: The U.S. Navy disabled an oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman, prompting a diplomatic protest from India after crew members went missing.
cards.body:
Three Indian sailors went missing after a U.S. Navy strike hit the tanker Settebello in the Gulf of Oman. Twenty-one crew members were rescued following the incident. The U.S. military said it targeted the vessel because it was transporting Iranian oil in violation of a blockade on Iranian ports.

India's government protested the strike and worked to locate the missing sailors. The incident underscores ongoing tensions over international shipping in the Gulf of Oman as the U.S. enforces restrictions on Iranian oil exports through this critical global energy route.

cards.headline: Trump Says U.S. Not Looking to Renew Trade Deal With Canada and Mexico
cards.teaser: The president said he does not intend to renew the free trade agreement with Canada and Mexico as talks continue between the three countries.
cards.body:
President Trump stated the U.S. is not seeking to renew the trade agreement with Canada and Mexico. He made the comments during ongoing negotiations between the three countries over their free-trade pact's renewal.

The timing of Trump's statement comes as the agreement approaches its deadline. The pact currently governs trade flows between the North American nations.

cards.headline: Senior Russian Military Official Killed in Car Explosion Near Moscow
cards.teaser: A high-ranking Russian military officer died in a car bombing outside Moscow in what appeared to be a targeted assassination.
cards.body: A senior Russian military official was killed in a car explosion near Moscow. The death appeared to be part of a series of targeted assassinations of high-profile opponents of Ukraine inside Russia, though no group has claimed responsibility for the attack. The killing comes as Ukraine has carried out or been linked to a string of attacks on Russian military and government figures on Russian soil, though Ukrainian officials typically do not confirm involvement in such operations.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise on Middle East Strikes and Trump Threats
cards.teaser: Fresh attacks strain a two-month cease-fire between Iran and the United States, jolting energy markets.
cards.body:
Oil prices climbed as Iran and Israel exchanged attacks, disrupting a two-month cease-fire between Iran and the United States. The military escalation has unsettled energy markets that had experienced relative calm during the truce period.

The Middle East remains a critical region for global oil production and shipping routes, making it particularly sensitive to geopolitical tensions. Markets across Asia also faced pressure from the renewed conflict alongside a technology sector sell-off.

cards.headline: Indonesian Military Court Sentences Four in Acid Attack on Rights Advocate
cards.teaser: Four people were sentenced by a military court for an acid attack on an outspoken critic of Indonesia's military.
cards.body:
An Indonesian military court sentenced four people in connection with an acid attack on a human rights advocate who has been an outspoken critic of the country's powerful military. Military prosecutors took over the case despite objections from the victim.

The victim had been vocal in challenging military conduct and accountability. The case raised questions about judicial independence when military courts handle crimes against civilians, particularly those who have criticized military institutions.

cards.headline: Violence Erupts in Belfast Following Stabbing Attack
cards.teaser: Cars and a bus were set on fire and families were forced from their homes after a stabbing sparked tensions in Belfast.
cards.body:
A stabbing attack sparked unrest across Belfast, with cars and a bus set ablaze and residents forced to evacuate their homes as communal tensions escalated into street violence.

The disorder rippled beyond Belfast into Glasgow, where police reported members of the public were attacked based on their race. A security adviser described the Belfast violence as "destabilising" and noted that discussing immigration in relation to national security remained "absolutely legitimate."

hero.headline: Federal grand jury indicts pro-Palestinian activists at University of Michigan on conspiracy charges
hero.body:
A federal grand jury has indicted eight pro-Palestinian activists at the University of Michigan on conspiracy charges related to an alleged campaign targeting university leadership over the institution's ties to Israel, according to court documents made public this week.

The indictments follow an FBI investigation into what prosecutors characterize as a coordinated effort involving threats of violence. Federal agents conducted raids as part of the enforcement action, including at a residence in Ypsilanti. The case represents one of the first major federal prosecutions targeting pro-Palestinian campus activists on charges of this nature.

Prosecutors allege the defendants orchestrated a campaign designed to pressure the University of Michigan to sever its connections with Israel through threatening behavior. The charges focus on conspiracy allegations, though initial reports did not provide extensive details about the specific threats or the exact timeline of the alleged campaign.

The University of Michigan has been a significant location for pro-Palestine activism in recent years. Student demonstrators have called for the university to divest from companies with ties to Israel, drawing attention to broader national debates over campus protests and activism concerning the Middle East conflict.

Universities across the country have faced ongoing tension between protecting free speech and addressing concerns about intimidation and threatening behavior. Administrators have struggled to balance these competing interests while responding to activism on their campuses.

The federal charges carry the possibility of substantial prison sentences if the defendants are convicted. Civil liberties advocates have raised concerns about the use of conspiracy statutes in cases involving political activism, arguing that such prosecutions can discourage protected speech. These observers contend that broad conspiracy charges can have a chilling effect on legitimate political expression.

The defendants will face proceedings in federal court. Prosecutors will need to demonstrate the allegations of coordinated threatening behavior beyond a reasonable doubt to secure convictions. Defense teams have not yet filed detailed responses to the charges in publicly available records.

The indictments come as the nation continues to grapple with questions about how to address campus activism related to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The case reflects broader tensions between law enforcement efforts to prevent threats and violence, and concerns from civil rights organizations about protecting political speech and assembly rights.

The prosecution underscores the heightened federal attention being paid to activism on university campuses, particularly activism related to international conflicts. It remains unclear how other institutions may respond to similar activism on their own campuses in light of these federal charges.

cards.headline: Ben Stokes removed from England squad after London nightclub incident
cards.teaser: The England cricketer will miss the second Test against New Zealand, with Joe Root named interim captain.
cards.body:
Ben Stokes has been removed from England's squad for the second Test against New Zealand at The Oval after breaking the team curfew during celebrations following England's victory in the first Test on Sunday night. Gus Atkinson was also left out of the squad for the same incident.

Joe Root will captain England in the upcoming match. The ECB is continuing its investigation into the nightclub incident. Stokes is considering his future, meeting with his agent and advisers to decide whether to step down as captain or potentially end his international career.

cards.headline: Primary elections shape midterm matchups in Maine, South Carolina, and Nevada
cards.teaser: Voters in multiple states selected candidates for November's midterm elections.
cards.body:
Primary elections held Tuesday in Maine, South Carolina, Nevada, and North Dakota determined general election matchups for the November midterms. In Maine, Democrat Graham Platner won his party's gubernatorial primary and will advance to a runoff, overcoming recent political scandals to secure the nomination. The results showed continued Democratic unity behind Platner's candidacy.

In South Carolina, Representative Nancy Mace lost her primary race, marking a significant upset. The primaries across the four states produced mixed results for candidates aligned with former President Trump, who has maintained influence over Republican primary contests. The outcomes set the stage for competitive general election battles in several key races.

cards.headline: Veterinarians call for ban on over-the-counter flea treatments for pets
cards.teaser: Pet owners have traditionally been told to treat cats and dogs monthly as a preventative measure.
cards.body:
Veterinarians are advising that over-the-counter flea treatments for pets should be banned, marking a shift from longstanding guidance. Pet owners have historically received advice to treat their cats and dogs with flea prevention products every month as a standard precautionary practice.

The recommendation to restrict access to these treatments represents a change in professional veterinary guidance. The veterinary community's position suggests concerns about the current availability of flea prevention products without professional oversight, though specific safety or efficacy issues prompting the recommendation were not detailed.

cards.headline: Researchers discover five-million-year-old whale graveyard in Indian Ocean
cards.teaser: The fossil site exceeds anything scientists had anticipated finding in the region.
cards.body:
Scientists have found the oldest, deepest and most extensive whale graveyard ever documented in the south-eastern Indian Ocean. Fossils at the site date back more than five million years to the Pliocene epoch.

The necropolis is remarkable for its extreme depth, extending beyond 7 kilometers below the surface—far deeper than typical whale falls, which usually occur at depths under 4 kilometers. The site stretches hundreds of miles across the ocean floor, revealing species and ecosystems previously unknown to science.

cards.headline: Three arrested in Glasgow after racist assaults following Belfast knife attack
cards.teaser: Police Scotland said members of the public were attacked because of the color of their skin.
cards.body:
Police Scotland arrested three people following unrest and racist assaults in Glasgow on Tuesday evening. Members of the public were attacked specifically because of the colour of their skin, according to officers.

The violence in Glasgow came after a knife attack in Belfast earlier that day, which triggered wider disorder across Northern Ireland. A terror adviser told the BBC that the disorder was "destabilising" and said it was legitimate to discuss immigration in relation to national security.

cards.headline: Belfast residents forced from homes during night of disorder after knife attack
cards.teaser: Violence erupted in Northern Ireland following a knife attack in the north of the city.
cards.body:
A knife attack in north Belfast triggered a night of widespread violence that forced residents to evacuate their homes. Disorder spread across Belfast and other parts of Northern Ireland, with fires set to houses, vehicles, and a bus during the protests.

Residents who fled described the trauma of watching their homes burn. A government terror adviser described the disorder as "destabilising," noting it was legitimate to discuss immigration in relation to national security concerns.

cards.headline: Trump Says He Loves Inflation as Prices Hit Three-Year High
cards.teaser: The president insists his agenda is working despite consumer prices rising faster than worker wages.
cards.body:
President Trump claimed he loves inflation as consumer prices reached their highest level in three years, with the Consumer Price Index hitting 4.2 percent. He attributed the price increases to U.S. actions against Iran, specifically seizing Iranian oil assets.

The national average gas price stands at about $4.16 per gallon—roughly $1 higher than a year earlier, though down $0.37 from a month ago. Trump has downplayed fuel costs as "not very high, relatively speaking," even as Americans face mounting affordability concerns from price surges linked to his administration's Iran policy.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Could Create 4,400 Employee Millionaires
cards.teaser: The rocket company's planned market debut is set to transform the financial lives of current and former workers.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for a highly anticipated stock market debut that could reshape the aerospace industry and create significant wealth for its workforce. An estimated 4,400 employees stand to become millionaires through their accumulated equity stakes, with the IPO providing the first opportunity for many to convert these holdings into liquid assets.

Elon Musk will see the greatest financial gain from the public offering. Much of SpaceX's valuation reflects investor enthusiasm for the company's ambitious space data center initiatives, which represent a substantial portion of the firm's projected value.

cards.headline: Artificial Intelligence Firms Raise Cash at Fastest Pace in Decades
cards.teaser: Companies like SpaceX and Alphabet are borrowing and raising equity to fund the race for AI dominance.
cards.body:
Artificial intelligence companies are raising money from investors at the fastest pace in decades as they compete to dominate the rapidly expanding industry. Major firms including SpaceX and Alphabet are both borrowing cash and raising equity capital to fund their AI ambitions.

The voracious appetite for capital reflects the massive infrastructure investments required to build and train advanced AI systems. Companies are rushing to secure funding while investor enthusiasm for the technology remains high, with billions of dollars flowing into the sector across both public and private markets.

cards.headline: Middle-Class Back Office Jobs Face AI Threat
cards.teaser: Millions of positions in human resources, billing, and payroll could be at risk as automation spreads.
cards.body:
Artificial intelligence is increasingly targeting middle-class back office jobs in fields like human resources, billing, and payroll, putting millions of positions at risk. Most of these jobs are held by women, raising concerns about the technology's disparate impact across the workforce.

The shift represents a new phase in AI adoption, moving beyond high-profile applications to everyday administrative and clerical work. Unlike previous waves of automation that primarily affected manufacturing, these white-collar positions have long been considered relatively secure from technological displacement.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall as Inflation Data Weighs on Tech Shares
cards.teaser: The Dow and Nasdaq opened lower after the Consumer Price Index showed prices rising to 4.2 percent.
cards.body:
Major stock indexes opened lower following the release of inflation data showing consumer prices rose to 4.2 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 700 points in early trading, while the Nasdaq also declined as technology stocks retreated.

The market selloff reflected investor concerns about the implications of higher inflation for Federal Reserve policy and corporate earnings. Technology shares led the decline, with traders reassessing valuations in light of the likelihood that interest rates will remain elevated for longer than previously expected.

hero.headline: German court rules against Google's AI search overviews
hero.body:
A German court ruled against Google's use of artificial intelligence in search results, a decision that could have widespread implications for the AI search industry. The court determined that AI-generated search overviews are not necessary for internet searches.

The ruling challenges Google's integration of AI Overview features into its search engine, which the company has been expanding across its platforms. Google AI Overviews provide automated summaries of search queries using large language models, appearing at the top of search results pages.

The German court's decision marks a significant legal setback for Google's AI search strategy in Europe. The ruling comes as tech companies have invested heavily in generative AI tools to enhance search capabilities and compete in the rapidly evolving search market. Google has positioned AI Overviews as a key feature to improve user experience and maintain its dominant position in search.

The court's determination that users do not need AI to search the internet questions the fundamental value proposition of AI-enhanced search tools. This legal precedent in Germany, Europe's largest economy, could influence regulatory approaches in other jurisdictions and affect how other companies deploy similar AI search features.

The ruling arrives at a time when the AI search industry faces growing scrutiny over accuracy, copyright concerns, and the value of AI-generated content. The decision may force Google and competitors to reconsider their AI search strategies in European markets and could slow the adoption of AI-powered search features globally. Other tech companies including Microsoft, which has integrated AI into its Bing search engine, may also need to evaluate their approaches in light of this precedent.

cards.headline: NASA announces crew for Artemis III moon mission planned for 2027
cards.teaser: NASA revealed the astronauts who will join the Artemis III mission, the agency's next step in returning humans to the lunar surface.
cards.body:
NASA has announced the crew for the Artemis III mission, scheduled to launch in 2027. The crew includes NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, and Andre Douglas, along with Luca Parmitano from the European Space Agency. During the mission, these four will orbit Earth while practicing docking procedures with their Orion capsule and two lunar landers.

This announcement represents the next phase in NASA's Artemis program, which aims to return astronauts to the moon. The mission builds on the success of Artemis II, which recently completed a record-breaking journey around the moon, surpassing the distance achieved by Apollo 13.

cards.headline: Scientists discover extensive whale graveyard five million years old in Indian Ocean
cards.teaser: Researchers found the deepest and most extensive whale graveyard ever recorded at the bottom of the Indian Ocean off Australia.
cards.body:
Scientists have found the oldest, deepest and most extensive whale graveyard ever discovered in the south-eastern Indian Ocean. The fossil remains, located in the Diamantina fracture zone, date back more than 5 million years and reach depths exceeding 7 kilometres—far deeper than the typical whale falls usually found at less than 4 kilometres.

The necropolis stretches hundreds of miles across the sea floor and contains skeletal remains of species and ecosystems previously unknown to science. This discovery provides researchers with unprecedented insight into ancient whale populations, migration patterns, and ocean conditions from millions of years ago.

cards.headline: India halts Starlink expansion plans ahead of SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: The Indian government reversed course on Starlink's operations in the country just before SpaceX's planned initial public offering.
cards.body:
India's government withdrew support for Starlink's expansion just before SpaceX's planned IPO. The regulatory reversal creates headwinds for the company's public offering, as India represents a major market opportunity for satellite internet services.

SpaceX's IPO valuation relies heavily on ambitious plans beyond its core Starlink business, particularly space-based data center concepts. The setback in India adds uncertainty to the company's international expansion narrative as it seeks to attract investors.

cards.headline: Companies spending heavily on AI allocate $7,500 per employee monthly
cards.teaser: Firms most committed to artificial intelligence spend roughly $7,500 per employee each month on AI tools and services, according to new spending data.
cards.body:
The most AI-focused companies are spending roughly $7,500 per employee monthly on artificial intelligence, according to the Ramp AI Index. This represents a substantial financial commitment as organizations integrate AI tools across their operations. While this spending level remains below typical engineer salaries, it underscores the significant resources being allocated to AI adoption.

The monthly expenditure covers AI tools, services, and infrastructure needed to support widespread employee use of generative AI and machine learning applications. The data illustrates how quickly AI-related costs are accumulating for companies that have made artificial intelligence central to their operations.

cards.headline: Apple releases iOS 27 with changes to volume controls and interface
cards.teaser: Apple's iOS 27 update introduces changes to core iPhone features that alter user interface patterns established over 15 years.
cards.body:
Apple released iOS 27 with a redesigned volume control feature that disrupts longstanding iPhone and iPad interface patterns established over 15 years. The update modifies how users adjust device volume, breaking familiar muscle memory for longtime Apple device users.

The new volume control addresses a frequently requested feature from users across multiple iOS generations. Early testers have responded positively to certain aspects of the update, Apple's annual mobile operating system refresh.

cards.headline: Medical groups release independent vaccine schedule rejecting federal changes
cards.teaser: OB-GYNs published their own vaccination schedule after disagreements with federal health policy direction.
cards.body:
Obstetricians and gynecologists released an independent vaccine schedule that rejects recent federal policy changes. Thirteen other medical organizations have endorsed the physician-created schedule, demonstrating broad support within the medical community. The move represents a direct response to vaccine policy adjustments made at the federal level.

The independent schedule provides healthcare providers with alternative guidance separate from current federal recommendations. The endorsement by multiple medical groups indicates significant concern within the healthcare community about the direction of national vaccine policy.

hero.headline: USMNT defender Richards clears injury, ready for World Cup opener against Paraguay
hero.teaser: Chris Richards says his ankle has healed sufficiently for him to play in Friday's match.
hero.body:
United States men's national team defender Chris Richards is working to recover from an ankle injury sustained during Crystal Palace's Premier League season, hoping to be available when the USMNT faces Paraguay in its World Cup Group D opener on Friday.

Richards suffered the injury in Crystal Palace's second-to-last league match against Brentford, which involved torn ligaments in his ankle. He missed the team's final Premier League fixture against Arsenal and did not play in the Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano.

Head coach Mauricio Pochettino has been cautiously optimistic about Richards's recovery timeline but remains noncommittal about his participation in the tournament opener. During a pre-match press conference, Pochettino said the team would need to assess Richards further before making a final decision about his availability.

"We are never going to take a decision to play with some player that has a minimum risk," Pochettino said. "We prefer to not take a risk. That's why all of the players that are going to start, or players that are going to come from the bench, it's because they are healthy, and they are 100% fit to play."

Richards represents a significant asset to the American squad. He is considered a key centerback option and is among the most important players on the roster. His potential absence would force Pochettino to rely on alternative defensive arrangements.

The defender has begun returning to training with the full squad following his rehabilitation period. During a recent session at the National Training Center, Richards participated partially with his teammates during warm-up activities but spent additional time working on lateral motion with trainers using resistance band exercises on a separate field.

Pochettino acknowledged frustration with the extended recovery timeline. Originally, there were indications Richards might feature in the Conference League final, which raised hopes about his World Cup readiness. Those projections have shifted as the healing process has taken longer than initially expected.

"In the end, we can hope that Chris can be there," Pochettino said. "But in the end, we're going to find ourselves with a player who's coming without competing for a month, and after, we have to make the decision if he's in form to compete or not."

If Richards is unavailable, the USMNT has backup options. During recent matches, Mark McKenzie played at the center of the defensive formation, while Tim Ream lined up on the left side and Alex Freeman served as additional defensive cover. Pochettino selected five centerbacks for his 26-man roster, providing depth in case Richards cannot participate.

World Cup regulations allow teams to make medically related squad changes until 24 hours before their group-stage opener. Pochettino has until June 11 to finalize whether Richards will remain part of his tournament plans as the Americans prepare for what is expected to be a competitive Group D campaign.

cards.headline: U.S. women's soccer team defeats Brazil 1-0 in match marred by eight red cards
cards.teaser: The United States women's national soccer team secured a 1-0 victory over Brazil in Fortaleza on Tuesday night in an unusually physical match that saw the home .
cards.body:
The United States women's national team won 1-0 against Brazil in Fortaleza on Tuesday night, with Sophia Wilson forcing an own goal in the second half. The match turned contentious, resulting in eight red cards issued to Brazil players. Brazil's head coach Arthur Elias and three staff members were also dismissed late in the second half, leaving the home team with nine players by full-time.

The intensity of the confrontation escalated after the final whistle, with riot police surrounding match officials on the pitch. U.S. manager Emma Hayes described the experience as unforgettable, while Brazil's Marta criticized the referee for being the "main character" in the affair. The disciplinary issues dominated what would otherwise be considered a routine friendly between the two traditional powers.

cards.headline: Victoria Mboko knee injury threatens doubles match with Serena Williams
cards.teaser: The tennis player suffered the injury during her singles match at Queen's Club on Wednesday.
cards.body:
Victoria Mboko was forced to retire from her singles match against Karolina Pliskova at Queen's Club on Wednesday after sustaining a left knee injury. The injury now casts doubt on her doubles partnership with Serena Williams, scheduled for Thursday evening at the HSBC Championships in London.

Williams, 44, recently returned to competitive tennis and won her opening doubles match alongside Mboko on Tuesday. Her campaign at the grass-court tournament now hinges on Mboko's ability to compete in their next scheduled match.

cards.headline: LeBron James declares himself the greatest basketball player
cards.teaser: The NBA star said he would not take anyone over himself in the GOAT debate.
cards.body:
LeBron James addressed the ongoing debate about basketball's greatest player of all time, stating his position clearly. When asked for his take on the GOAT discussion, James said he would not take anyone over himself.

The declaration from James adds his own perspective to a debate that has persisted throughout his career and shows no signs of resolution. James has built a case through championships, individual accolades, and sustained excellence over more than two decades in the NBA.

cards.headline: Colts receiver Alec Pierce may miss training camp after ankle surgery
cards.teaser: Pierce's recovery could extend well into training camp and past the preseason.
cards.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce is expected to miss training camp while recovering from ankle surgery. His rehabilitation timeline could extend beyond the preseason as well.

The injury creates a significant gap in the Colts' receiving corps as the team enters the offseason program and prepares for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Giants coach Harbaugh optimistic about Malik Nabers return
cards.teaser: John Harbaugh said he is hopeful the wide receiver will be back soon based on recent progress.
cards.body:
New York Giants coach John Harbaugh expressed optimism about wide receiver Malik Nabers' return to action. Harbaugh said he is "hopeful" the receiver will be back soon, citing the progress Nabers has made recently.

The Giants are eager to have Nabers back in the lineup as they look ahead in their season.

cards.headline: Texas Tech athletic director addresses quarterback Sorsby's gambling addiction recovery
cards.teaser: Kirby Hocutt issued a statement supporting Brendan Sorsby while leaving open the possibility of him playing this season.
cards.body:
Texas Tech athletic director Kirby Hocutt released a lengthy statement on Wednesday addressing quarterback Brendan Sorsby's situation. Hocutt said he continues to support Sorsby's recovery from an admitted gambling addiction while acknowledging there is no perfect answer to the circumstances.

Hocutt did not rule out the possibility of Sorsby playing during the upcoming season. The athletic director's statement attempted to balance support for the player's personal recovery with the complex decisions facing the football program regarding his status on the team.

hero.headline: Academy to Honor Glenn Close, Ridley Scott, Floyd Norman with Honorary Oscars
hero.body:
The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has announced Honorary Oscars for actress Glenn Close, director Ridley Scott, and animator Floyd Norman. Producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler will receive the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award. The Academy's Board of Governors voted to bestow these recognitions on the five honorees.

Close will finally receive an Oscar after eight nominations throughout her career. She has been recognized for roles in Fatal Attraction, Dangerous Liaisons, and Hillbilly Elegy. The Academy described her as an actor with an "unparalleled emotional range" who has "brought to life some of the most complex characters in cinema."

Scott, who has directed influential films across science fiction and historical drama, has received four Oscar nominations. His acclaimed work includes Thelma & Louise and Gladiator. The Academy called him "a true visionary whose decades-long legacy has left an immeasurable impact on global cinema and culture."

Norman, now 90 years old, made history as Disney's first Black animator. His uncredited work appeared in early Disney classics including The Jungle Book and Sleeping Beauty, while later credited roles included Monsters Inc and Alvin and the Chipmunks. The Academy praised him as someone who has "inspired generations of artists over his remarkable career."

Vachon and Koffler, who founded Killer Films, have championed independent cinema for decades. They recently earned their first Oscar nomination for producing the romantic drama Past Lives. Their production company credits also include Boys Don't Cry, May December, and Materialists.

The Honorary Oscar recognizes "extraordinary distinction in lifetime achievement, exceptional contributions to the state of motion picture arts and sciences in any discipline, or for outstanding service to the Academy." This award has been presented by the Academy since 1929 and remains separate from the main Oscar telecast.

The ceremony will take place on November 15. Recipients join a prestigious group of honorees celebrated for their career achievements and contributions to the motion picture industry. Last year's recipients included Tom Cruise and Dolly Parton.

Close's next film role will appear in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping later this year. Scott's post-apocalyptic thriller The Dog Stars is scheduled for release in August.

cards.headline: Tyler Mane Reveals Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Urges Men to Get Checked
cards.teaser: The former wrestler and X-Men actor disclosed his breast cancer diagnosis and is encouraging men to seek medical screening.
cards.body:
Tyler Mane, known for his roles in X-Men and Halloween and his career as a professional wrestler, announced he has been diagnosed with breast cancer. The actor shared the news publicly, using the platform to raise awareness about the disease in men.

Mane is urging men to get checked for breast cancer, a disease often associated primarily with women but that also affects male patients. Breast cancer in men is rare, accounting for a small fraction of all breast cancer cases. The actor's disclosure aims to increase awareness and encourage screening among male populations.

cards.headline: CAA and TPG Form $250 Million Company to Buy Creator-Led Businesses
cards.teaser: The talent agency and private equity firm launched Compound Creative Holdings to acquire and operate companies led by YouTubers and digital creators.
cards.body:
CAA partnered with TPG's Integrated Media Company to establish Compound Creative Holdings, a $250 million holding company focused on the creator economy. The venture will acquire, operate, and grow businesses led by online content creators including YouTubers.

The partnership reunites CAA with TPG, which previously held a majority ownership stake in the talent agency. The holding company targets the expanding creator economy, where individual content producers have built substantial businesses around their online presence and audiences. The venture represents institutional investment in digital content creation as a business sector.

cards.headline: AMC Theatres Delays Concert Simulcasts After Summer Box Office Surge
cards.teaser: The cinema chain postponed live concert broadcasts from Bebe Rexha, Paris Hilton, and other performers following stronger-than-expected film releases.
cards.body:
AMC Theatres has postponed its plans to simulcast live concerts featuring Bebe Rexha, Paris Hilton, Kim Petras, and Maren Morris. The decision reflects a shift in the cinema chain's programming strategy.

The postponement comes as AMC responded to stronger-than-expected summer box office performance, prompting the theater chain to revise its content lineup to capitalize on the theatrical momentum.

cards.headline: Adam Friedland to Bring Talk Show to Spotify in July
cards.teaser: The comedian will relaunch The Adam Friedland Show on Spotify with ad sales and distribution across podcast platforms.
cards.body:
Comedian Adam Friedland announced The Adam Friedland Show will move to Spotify when its third season launches in July. The streaming service will handle ad sales and distribute the talk show across all podcast platforms.

Friedland also plans a World Cup-focused series with The Ringer. The comedian said he is excited about the partnership, though he noted his request for a Spotify premium membership as part of the deal. The talk show will continue its format while gaining access to Spotify's distribution network and advertising infrastructure.

cards.headline: Edgar Ramirez Joins Cast of Task Season 2 at HBO
cards.teaser: The actor will appear alongside returning star Mark Ruffalo and newly added cast members including Mahershala Ali.
cards.body:
Edgar Ramirez has been cast in the second season of Task at HBO. He joins Mark Ruffalo, who returns from the first season, along with new additions Mahershala Ali, Harry Melling, Adam Nagaitis, and Aminah Nieves.

The new season follows Tom Brandis, played by Ruffalo, as he takes the helm of an operation. HBO has not disclosed additional plot details or premiere timing for the second season. The show continues to build its ensemble cast with established film and television actors.

cards.headline: Sydney Sweeney Reflects on Final Euphoria Season, Cassie's Arc
cards.teaser: The actress, who earned an Emmy nomination in 2022, said she still thinks about where her character might have gone beyond the series finale.
cards.body:
Sydney Sweeney discussed her work on the third and final season of Euphoria, saying she dove even deeper into her character Cassie Howard than in previous seasons. Sweeney, who received an Emmy nomination for the second season in 2022, told Variety she remains unsatisfied with where Cassie's story concluded.

The actress addressed being sexualized in the series and emotional moments including Rue's death. She said she continues to think about what else Cassie might have experienced beyond the show's ending. The HBO drama wrapped its run after three seasons exploring the lives of teenagers navigating addiction, relationships, and identity.

hero.headline: US military disables oil tanker in Gulf of Oman, India reports crew missing
hero.teaser: The US military disabled an oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman on Tuesday after determining the vessel violated an ongoing US naval blockade, US Central Command ann.
hero.body:
The US military struck the oil tanker Settebello in the Gulf of Oman on Tuesday after determining it violated a US naval blockade, according to US Central Command's announcement Wednesday. The strike disabled the vessel off the coast of Oman.

India reported that three of its sailors went missing following the incident, while 21 crew members were rescued. The disappearances have prompted diplomatic objections from the Indian government over the military action and the fate of its citizens.

cards.headline: House committee questions NFL executives over streaming costs
cards.teaser: Lawmakers from both parties criticized the NFL over rising costs for watching televised games at a House Judiciary Committee hearing.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Members of the House Judiciary Committee challenged NFL representatives Wednesday over the increasing expense of watching games as the league moves toward streaming deals. Lawmakers from both parties argued that their constituents face financial burdens due to the changing broadcast landscape.

Republicans and Democrats said the shift to streaming has created what they consider an anticompetitive economic environment. The hearing focused on how the NFL's new distribution arrangements affect fans who previously relied on traditional broadcast and cable television to watch games.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided covers unrelated stories (GB News climate donations and a UFC champion's White House access) and does not contain information about the NFL hearing or streaming costs. Therefore, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Rep. Mace to leave Congress for private sector
cards.teaser: Rep. Nancy Mace said she will return to the private sector when her term ends in January 2027 after failing to advance in South Carolina's GOP gubernatorial primary.
cards.body:
Rep. Nancy Mace of South Carolina announced Wednesday that she will return to the private sector once her congressional term concludes in January 2027. The Republican representative said she was headed back to the private sector at the end of this term, as the Founders intended.

The announcement followed her failure to advance to a runoff in the Republican gubernatorial primary in South Carolina. Mace had sought the governor's office but did not secure enough votes to continue in the race. She has represented South Carolina in the House but will not seek reelection to her congressional seat.

cards.headline: House committee to investigate Epstein connections
cards.teaser: Alan Dershowitz said he wants complete transparency if called to testify before the House Oversight Committee about Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
Representative James Comer, chair of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, announced Wednesday that he will ask Alan Dershowitz, Jeffrey Epstein's former attorney, to testify as part of the panel's investigation into the late sex offender. Comer said the decision was based on testimony from Lesley Groff, Epstein's longtime assistant, who appeared before the committee Tuesday, as well as meetings with Epstein survivors.

Dershowitz stated he wants complete transparency if he testifies before the committee. The investigation examines matters related to Epstein and individuals connected to him.

cards.headline: CFTC proposes regulations for prediction markets
cards.teaser: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission introduced new rules to clarify what types of events can be traded on prediction market platforms.
cards.body:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission proposed new regulations Wednesday for prediction markets, aiming to define what types of events can be listed for trading. The proposal seeks to specify which events the agency considers contrary to the public interest and therefore ineligible for listing on trading platforms.

The Trump administration's proposal represents an effort to establish clearer regulatory boundaries for the growing prediction market industry. The CFTC oversees commodity futures trading and has jurisdiction over certain types of event contracts traded on these platforms.

cards.headline: Poll shows majority of Americans worried about AI job losses
cards.teaser: A Reuters/Ipsos survey found 53 percent of respondents fear they or someone in their household will lose a job because of artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
More than half of Americans surveyed in a new Reuters/Ipsos poll expressed worry that artificial intelligence will lead to job losses in their households. The survey of 4,531 respondents conducted in early June found that 53 percent felt concerned about AI's impact on employment. Meanwhile, 37 percent said they were not worried about such losses.

The poll reflects broader public anxiety about how AI technologies will reshape the job market across different industries and sectors.

cards.headline: OB-GYN group issues vaccine guidance differing from CDC
cards.teaser: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists released a maternal vaccine schedule that diverges from CDC recommendations for the first time.
cards.body:
The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists released a recommended maternal vaccine schedule Wednesday that differs from guidance issued by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. This marks the first time the professional organization has broken with CDC recommendations on this topic.

ACOG recommended four vaccines be administered during pregnancy: a flu shot, a COVID-19 shot, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis, and one to protect against respiratory syncytial virus in the developing fetus. The organization also provided additional recommendations for maternal vaccination timing and protocols.
